comment: Each shot names the elements clicked to reach it, in order, one per frame.
They are element ids in the exported menu.rml, clicked through the bridge's
own listeners — the same path a player's pointer takes. An id that is not
in the document stops the run rather than screenshotting the wrong screen.
A step written "wait:120" waits that many frames instead, which is how
anything on a clock is photographed at a chosen moment.
A shot that needs a different game says so beside its script: the boot
notice does not exist in an export that opens at the menu, because the
player is already looking at the menu. A shot may also name settings its
run needs; `pause_nonactive` is how the emulated console keeps running
while its window sits in the background, which it always does here.
These are the same states scripts/fixtures/menu-states.json declares, but
reached rather than posed: menu-states sets the classes itself, and cannot
show that pressing CONTROLS gets you to the controls screen.
